claims.text: Under the 2023 Federal Reserve severely adverse scenario, the aggregate CET1 ratio of the 23 tested banks fell from an actual 12.4 percent (2022:Q4) to a projected minimum of 9.9 percent, then rose to 10.5 percent at the end of the projection horizon (2025:Q1).

citations.quotation:
Under the severely adverse scenario, the aggregate CET1 capital ratio of the 23 banks falls from
an actual 12.4 percent in the fourth quarter of 2022 to its minimum of 9.9 percent, before rising
to 10.5 percent at the end of the projection

claims.text: Both aggregate and individual banks' post-stress CET1 ratios remained well above required minimum levels throughout the projection horizon.

citations.quotation:
The aggregate and individual bank post-stress
common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital ratios remain well above the required minimum levels
throughout the projection horizon.

counterarguments.text: The stress test is only a projection, not a guarantee: the decline from 12.4% to 9.9% shows substantial capital depletion (~2.5 percentage points), so a more severe scenario than the modeled one could bring banks closer to minimums. Actual performance under real stress may differ from projected results.
